one_liner: Pumble has a free, self-serve REST API (API-key addon plus OAuth2 app SDK) and an official hosted MCP server. A toolkit is buildable now.
auth_notes: Pumble apps use an OAuth2 authorization-code flow (code exchange with client-id/client-secret); requests also need an x-app-token header. The API Keys addon gives a static bearer key with a narrower API, and Composio's existing toolkit uses API_KEY. Creating an app is self-serve through Configure apps. The OAuth auth_primary is only medium-confidence given the app-install step.
access_notes: The API addon is available on all plans, including Free. The Free plan allows up to 3 addons. Only Owners and Admins can install apps, so the builder must own or admin a workspace (easy to create free).
blocker_notes: Minor: the OAuth app requires a public HTTP server for events, and the API key addon has limited endpoints. Neither blocks a toolkit.

evidence.quote: you must first generate an API key within your Pumble workspace administration panel. This token must be passed inside the HTTP header of every request as a bearer token.
It's mandatory to include the token (access token issued to user/bot) and x-app-token (app token issued to your app, prefixed with 'xpat-') headers in every request
A Pumble workspace where you are allowed to install apps. The free Pumble plan is enough.
Only Owners and Admins can install apps.
This addon lets you generate an API key that allows you to send messages, reactions, and more via simple HTTP requests.
Pumble maintains a native MCP (Model Context Protocol) server hosted directly at pumble.com, helping you connect your workspace to your AI agent of choice.
